subject: Admin activity extract & signed manifest — export options and redaction recipe
messages:
From: Liam O'Donnell <liam.odonnell@acmepharma.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: admin activity extract for SIG/CAIQ review

Hi Priya,

We're preparing for an upcoming SIG/CAIQ review and need a reproducible export of Redwood's admin activity for Acme Pharmaceuticals. Scope is 12 months (May 2027 → May 2028). Specifically we need:
- all admin events (role changes, user creation/deletion, group membership updates)
- API key and service token creation/usage events (including key id, creation timestamp, last-used timestamp)
- operator session starts/stops and elevated session metadata
- model-serving control-plane actions (deploy, rollback, pin/version changes)
- any attacker-detection flags or emergency access events

Delivery requirements:
- Signed manifest (sha256 checksums per file; manifest itself should be signed by Redwood's export certificate)
- Chain-of-custody notes (who prepared, who approved, UTC timestamps)
- PII redaction guidance: we cannot receive raw email addresses or full API tokens, but stable hashed identifiers are acceptable if reversible only by Redwood. If you do hashing, please include the salt management approach.
- Delivery target: secure S3 bucket (we will provide a customer-managed bucket + KMS key).

Can you confirm what you can provide, the format (JSONL/Parquet), expected timeline, and any limitations (sampling, retention windows, cross-region normalization)?

Thanks,
Liam O'Donnell
Head of Compliance — Acme Pharmaceuticals
compliance@acmepharma.com

---
Attachment: acme_evidence_requirements.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.example>
To: Liam O'Donnell <liam.odonnell@acmepharma.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity extract for SIG/CAIQ review

Liam — thanks for the clear scope. We can support this and have two delivery patterns depending on Acme's preference:

1) Snapshot bundle (recommended for audit evidence):
   - Format: gzipped JSONL files (one file per event-type) + a top-level signed manifest (sha256 checksums).
   - Redaction: field-level deterministic salted hashing for PII (email, user external ids). Salt is stored in our HSM; we can provide per-hash metadata but not the raw salt.
   - Timeline: preliminary 4 business days for a 90-day snapshot; full 12-month run typically 10–12 business days (depends on volume).

2) Direct-to-bucket streaming export (recommended if you expect replays):
   - We stream events to a customer S3 prefix using temporary credentials (assume-role) and multipart uploads. Each chunk is checksummed and we publish a manifest per-hour.
   - Pro: minimal downtime, easy re-ingest. Con: work to verify end-to-end checksums during transfer.

Notes/limits:
- We normalize all timestamps to UTC ISO8601 and include the original timezone offset when available.
- Operator session payloads exclude keystroke-level telemetry; we include session start/end and privilege escalations.
- For API keys we will not deliver raw secrets; only key ids and last-used metadata.

Attachments: sample_manifest_template.txt, redaction_policy.md (stubs attached).

If this works, please confirm acceptance and whether you want snapshot or streaming. Also confirm the S3 bucket/KMS details and a contact for verifying manifests.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Security & Compliance (Redwood Inference)
priya.natarajan@redwood.example

Liam / Priya — technical notes from runtime/infra:

1) Event selection and query recipes:
   - role_change: SELECT * FROM admin_events WHERE type = 'role_change' AND timestamp BETWEEN ... ORDER BY timestamp asc
   - api_key_events: includes fields {key_id, actor_id, created_at, last_used_at, scopes} (no token material)

2) Redaction recipe (recommended):
   - deterministic HMAC-SHA256 with per-customer salt (format: HMAC_SHA256(base64salt, field_value))
   - we will publish "salt-version" in the manifest and rotate per-export; reversible only by Redwood under legal/auth access.

3) Manifest format (sample):
   {file: events/role_change-20270501_20280501.jsonl.gz, sha256: abcd..., records: 1,234}

4) Timezones: normalize to UTC and include original_tz field where available.

5) Integrity and chain-of-custody: we will sign the manifest with the export certificate (X.509) and include a signed metadata file with preparer/approver names and UTC timestamps.

Attachments: redaction_script.py (tiny script showing HMAC example).

Soojin
Principal, Production Security (Redwood Inference)

Adding infra details and a small manifest example. When we do a direct-to-bucket export we'll use an assume-role flow with limited-scope temporary credentials that expire after the job completes. Upload notes:
- Recommended KMS: alias/redwood/evidence-exports or accept customer's KMS key (we prefer customer-managed).
- Multipart upload chunk size: 100 MiB. Finalize with ETag + sha256 in manifest.

Sample manifest entry (plain text):
file: events/api_key_events-20270501_20280501.jsonl.gz
sha256: 3b7f2d1c4a...
records: 23,452
compressed_size: 1,234,567

We will also publish a signed "export-metadata.json" that includes: preparer (karthik.iyer@redwood.example), approver (priya.natarajan@redwood.example), prepared_at_utc, approved_at_utc, export_tool_version.
